**Type and Title of the Instrument:** Regulation (EU) 2019/26 of the European Parliament and of the Council

**Legal Basis:** Article 114 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union

**Subject Matter and Scope:** This Regulation complements Directive 2007/46/EC, Regulation (EU) No 167/2013, Regulation (EU) No 168/2013, and Regulation (EU) 2016/1628 by establishing special provisions for the EU type-approval and the placing on the market of vehicles, systems, components, and separate technical units which have been type-approved by the UK type-approval authority (UK type-approval) while the Union type-approval legislation still applies to and in the United Kingdom.

**Primary Obligations, Prohibitions, or Entitlements:** 

1. A manufacturer holding a UK type-approval that has not become invalid pursuant to Article 17 of Directive 2007/46/EC, Article 32 of Regulation (EU) No 167/2013, Article 37 of Regulation (EU) No 168/2013, or Article 30 of Regulation (EU) 2016/1628 may submit an application to a Union type-approval authority for a Union type-approval of the same type until Union type-approval legislation ceases to apply to and in the United Kingdom.

2. The Union type-approval authority may grant a Union type-approval if the type in question meets the requirements for the placing on the market, registration, or entry into service of new vehicles, systems, components, or separate technical units at the time when the Union type-approval takes effect.

3. The Union type-approval authority may request the repetition of specific tests if necessary, and may require new tests to be carried out by a technical service designated and notified by the Member State of the Union type-approval authority in accordance with Directive 2007/46/EC, Regulation (EU) No 167/2013, Regulation (EU) No 168/2013, or Regulation (EU) 2016/1628.

4. The Union type-approval shall take effect on the day of its granting or on a later date determined therein. The UK type-approval shall become invalid on the day preceding the day on which the Union type-approval takes effect. In any event, it shall become invalid at the latest on the day on which the Union type-approval legislation referred to in Article 2(1) ceases to apply to and in the United Kingdom.

5. The Union type-approval authority shall take full responsibility for the obligations stemming from the Union type-approval, including exercising all the powers and fulfilling all the obligations of the UK type-approval authority with respect to vehicles, systems, components, or separate technical units produced on the basis of the UK type-approval already placed on the market, registered, or entered into service in the Union.

6. The Union type-approval authority shall not be liable for any acts or omissions of the UK type-approval authority.

**Key Defined Terms:**

- Union type-approval authority: A type-approval authority of a Member State other than the United Kingdom
- UK type-approval: An EC type-approval or EU type-approval granted by the UK type-approval authority
- Union type-approval: An EU type-approval granted by a Union type-approval authority in accordance with this Regulation

**Entry into Force:** This Regulation shall enter into force on the third day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.

**Transitional and Sunset Provisions:** This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States. **Subject Matter and Scope:** This Regulation harmonizes the calculation of Gross National Income at Market Prices (GNI) across Member States, replacing the Council Directive 89/130/EEC, Euratom and Council Regulation (EC, Euratom) No 1287/2003 (GNI Regulation). It aims to ensure the comparability, reliability, and exhaustiveness of GNI data for own resources purposes, as defined in the European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010).

They must provide the Commission (Eurostat) with GNI data and a report on the quality of the data before 1 October each year. The Commission is tasked with verifying the sources and methods used to produce GNI data, establishing an inventory of these sources and methods, and adopting delegated acts to ensure the reliability, exhaustiveness, and comparability of GNI data. The Commission may conduct GNI information visits in Member States to verify compliance with ESA 2010 and to ensure the quality of GNI aggregates and their components.

**Key Defined Terms:** Gross National Income (GNI), Gross Domestic Product (GDP), and the European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010).

**Entry-into-Force Date:** 29.3.2019 (19 March 2019)

**Transitional or Sunset Provisions:** Directive 89/130/EEC, Euratom and Regulation (EC, Euratom) No 1287/2003 are repealed, and their references are replaced by this Regulation. The Commission's delegated powers under this Regulation are valid for 5 years from 18 April 2019, with the possibility of tacit extension or revocation by the European Parliament or the Council.

**Regulation (EU) 2019/1156 of the European Parliament and of the Council**

**Type and Title of the Instrument:** Regulation (EU) 2019/1156 of the European Parliament and of the Council

**Subject Matter and Scope:**
This Regulation establishes uniform rules on the publication of national provisions concerning marketing requirements for collective investment undertakings (AIFs) and UCITS, and on marketing communications addressed to investors. It also provides for common principles concerning fees and charges levied on managers of collective investment undertakings in relation to their cross-border activities. The Regulation applies to alternative investment fund managers (AIFMs), UCITS management companies, EuVECA managers, and EuSEF managers.

**Primary Obligations, Prohibitions, or Entitlements:**
1. Marketing communications addressed to investors must be identifiable as such and describe the risks and rewards of purchasing units or shares of an AIF or UCITS in an equally prominent manner. All information included in marketing communications must be fair, clear, and not misleading.
2. UCITS management companies must ensure that marketing communications containing specific information about a UCITS do not contradict or diminish the significance of the information contained in the prospectus or key investor information.
3. Marketing communications must specify where, how, and in which language investors can obtain summarised information on investor rights and clearly state that the manager or management company has the right to terminate the arrangements made for marketing.
4. AIFMs, EuVECA managers, and EuSEF managers must ensure that marketing communications comprising an invitation to purchase units or shares of an AIF do not contradict the information which is to be disclosed to the investors in accordance with Directive 2011/61/EU or Regulation (EU) No 345/2013.
5. Marketing communications must be published and maintained on the websites of competent authorities in a language customary in the sphere of international finance, and ESMA should create a central database containing summaries of national requirements for marketing communications and hyperlinks to the information published on the websites of competent authorities.

**Key Defined Terms:**

- Alternative investment fund managers (AIFMs)
- EuVECA manager
- EuSEF manager
- Competent authorities
- Home Member State
- UCITS
- UCITS management company

**Entry-into-Force Date:**
This Regulation enters into force on the twentieth day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union and applies from 1 August 2019. However, certain provisions, including those related to marketing communications and pre-marketing, apply from 2 August 2021.

The transitional exemption from the obligations under Regulation (EU) No 1286/2014 is prolonged by 24 months. The Commission shall also submit a report on reverse solicitation and demand on the own initiative of an investor by 2 August 2021. The application dates of national laws, regulations, and administrative provisions implementing Directive (EU) 2019/1160 and this Regulation shall be synchronised. The Regulation does not go beyond what is necessary to achieve its objective of enhancing market efficiency while establishing the capital markets union.

**Regulation (EU) 2019/1157 of the European Parliament and of the Council**

**Type and Title of the Instrument:** Regulation (EU) 2019/1157 of the European Parliament and of the Council

**Legal Basis:** Article 21(2) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU)

**Subject Matter and Scope:**
This Regulation strengthens the security standards applicable to identity cards issued by Member States to their nationals and to residence documents issued by Member States to Union citizens and their family members when exercising their right to free movement. It applies to identity cards issued by Member States to their own nationals as referred to in Article 4(3) of Directive 2004/38/EC, registration certificates issued in accordance with Article 8 of Directive 2004/38/EC to Union citizens residing for more than three months in a host Member State and documents certifying permanent residence issued in accordance with Article 19 of Directive 2004/38/EC to Union citizens upon application; residence cards issued in accordance with Article 10 of Directive 2004/38/EC to family members of Union citizens who are not nationals of a Member State and permanent residence cards issued in accordance with Article 20 of Directive 2004/38/EC to family members of Union citizens who are not nationals of a Member State.

**Key Obligations, Prohibitions, or Entitlements:**
- Identity cards must be produced in ID-1 format, contain a machine-readable zone (MRZ), and comply with the specifications and minimum security standards set out in ICAO Document 9303. They must include a facial image and two fingerprints in interoperable digital formats, and the biometric data must be stored in a highly secure manner.
- Residence documents must include specific information such as the title of the document, a clear reference that the document is issued to a Union citizen, the document number, the name (surname and forename(s)) of the holder, the date of birth of the holder, and the issuing authority.
- Residence cards for family members of Union citizens who are not nationals of a Member State must use the same format as established by Regulation (EC) No 1030/2002 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2017/1954 and comply with the specifications of ICAO Document 9303.
- Biometric data stored in the storage medium of identity cards and residence documents must be used only for verifying the authenticity of the document and the identity of the holder, and must be kept in a highly secure manner and only until the date of collection of the document and, in any case, no longer than 90 days from the date of issue.

**Key Defined Terms:**
- Identity card: A document issued by a Member State to its own nationals.
- Residence document: A document issued by a Member State to Union citizens and their family members when exercising their right to free movement.
- Residence card: A residence document issued to family members of Union citizens who are not nationals of a Member State.
- Biometric data: Facial image and two fingerprints stored on the secure storage medium of identity cards and residence documents.

**Entry-into-Force Date:** 2 August 2021

**Transitional or Sunset Provisions:** This Regulation applies from 2 August 2021, and existing identity cards and residence cards which do not meet the requirements set out in this Regulation shall cease to be valid at their expiry or by 3 August 2031, whichever is earlier. Identity cards which do not meet the minimum security standards set out in part 2 of ICAO document 9303 or which do not include a functional MRZ shall cease to be valid at their expiry or by 3 August 2026, whichever is earlier. Residence cards of family members of Union citizens who are not nationals of a Member State which do not meet the requirements of Article 7 shall cease to be valid at their expiry or by 3 August 2026, whichever is earlier. Residence cards of family members of Union citizens who are not nationals of a Member State which do not meet the minimum security standards set out in part 2 of ICAO document 9303 or which do not include a functional MRZ shall cease to be valid at their expiry or by 3 August 2023, whichever is earlier.

**Key Considerations:**
- The Regulation respects the fundamental rights and observes the principles recognized in particular by the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union.
- The Regulation does not affect the competence of the Member States to issue other residence documents which fall outside the scope of Union law.
- The Regulation does not prevent Member States from accepting, in a non-discriminatory manner, documents other than travel documents, for identification purposes, such as driving licences.
- The Regulation does not affect the use of identity cards and residence documents with eID function by Member States for other purposes, nor does it affect the rules laid down in Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

**Council Decision (CFSP) 2020/472 of 31 March 2020 on a European Union military operation in the Mediterranean (EUNAVFOR MED IRINI)**

**Type and Title of the Instrument:** Council Decision (CFSP) 2020/472

**Legal Basis:** Article 42(4) and 43(2) of the Treaty on European Union (TEU)

**Subject Matter and Scope of Application:**
The Council establishes and launches a military crisis management operation, EUNAVFOR MED IRINI, to contribute to preventing arms trafficking within its agreed Area of Operation and Area of Interest in accordance with UNSCR 1970 (2011) and subsequent Resolutions on the arms embargo on Libya, including UNSCR 2292 (2016) and UNSCR 2473 (2019). The operation shall also contribute to the implementation of UN measures to prevent the illicit export of petroleum from Libya in accordance with UNSCR 2146 (2014) and subsequent Resolutions, in particular UNSCR 2509 (2020) and UNSCR 2510 (2020). In addition, the operation shall assist in the development of the capacities and in the training of the Libyan Coast Guard and Navy in law enforcement tasks at sea. The operation shall also contribute to the disruption of the business model of human smuggling and trafficking networks, in accordance with applicable international law, including the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea, any relevant UNSCR, and international human rights law as applicable.

**Primary Obligations, Prohibitions, or Entitlements:**
1. EUNAVFOR MED IRINI shall, as its core task, contribute to the implementation of the UN arms embargo on Libya with aerial, satellite and maritime assets.
2. EUNAVFOR MED IRINI shall gather extensive and comprehensive information on the trafficking of arms and related materiel from all directions and share it with relevant partners and agencies on a case-by-case and need-to-know basis through the mechanisms in the relevant planning documents in order to contribute to a full situational awareness in the Area of Operation and in the Area of Interest. Where such information is classified up to ‘SECRET UE/EU SECRET’ level, it may be exchanged with relevant partners and agencies in accordance with Council Decision 2013/488/EU and based on arrangements concluded at the operational level in accordance with Article 14(9) of this Decision, and in full respect of the principles of reciprocity and inclusiveness. Classified information received shall be handled by EUNAVFOR MED IRINI without any distinction between its staff and solely on the basis of operational requirements.
3. EUNAVFOR MED IRINI shall carry out, in accordance with the arrangements set out in the planning documents, and within the agreed Area of Operation on the high seas off the coast of Libya, inspections of vessels bound to or from Libya where there are reasonable grounds to believe that such vessels are carrying arms or related materiel to or from Libya, directly or indirectly, in violation of the arms embargo on Libya. EUNAVFOR MED IRINI shall take relevant action to seize and dispose of such items, including with a view to diverting such vessels and their crews to a suitable port to facilitate such disposal, with the consent of the port State, in accordance with relevant UNSCRs including UNSCR 2292 (2016).
4. EUNAVFOR MED IRINI shall report to the Political and Security Committee (PSC) on all issues and events related to such inspections. The PSC may consider any subsequent measures, as appropriate.
5. In view of the exceptional operational requirements, and upon invitation from a Member State, EUNAVFOR MED IRINI may divert vessels to ports of that Member State and dispose within that Member State of arms and related materiel seized in accordance with paragraph 3, including by storage and destruction. The ports to which vessels may be diverted shall be designated in the Operations Plan.
6. EUNAVFOR MED IRINI may collect and store evidence related to the carriage of items prohibited under the arms embargo on Libya. EUNAVFOR MED IRINI may collect and store, in accordance with applicable law, personal data concerning persons involved in the carriage of such prohibited items, including fingerprints, as well as the following particulars, with the exclusion of other personal data: surname, maiden name, given names and any alias or assumed name; date and place of birth, nationality, sex, place of residence, profession and whereabouts; driving licenses, identification documents and passport data. EUNAVFOR MED IRINI may transmit such data as well as data related to the vessels and equipment used by such persons, and the relevant information acquired while carrying out this core task, to the relevant law enforcement authorities of Member States and to competent Union bodies in accordance with applicable law.
7. EUNAVFOR MED IRINI shall contribute to the implementation of the UN measures against illicit exports of petroleum from Libya as a secondary task, conducting monitoring and surveillance activities and gathering information on illicit exports from Libya of petroleum, including crude oil and refined petroleum products, which are contrary to UNSCR 2146 (2014) and subsequent UNSCRs, in particular UNSCR 2509 (2020), thereby contributing to situational awareness in the Area of Operation and in the Area of Interest.
8. EUNAVFOR MED IRINI shall assist in the development of the capacities and in the training of the Libyan Coast Guard and Navy in law enforcement tasks at sea, in particular to prevent human smuggling and trafficking, as a further secondary task.
9. EUNAVFOR MED IRINI shall support the detection and monitoring of human smuggling and trafficking networks through information gathering and patrolling carried out by aerial assets above the high seas, in the agreed Area of Operation.
10. EUNAVFOR MED IRINI shall cooperate with the relevant Member State authorities and shall establish a coordination mechanism, and, as appropriate, conclude arrangements with other Union agencies and bodies, in particular Frontex, EUROPOL, EUROJUST, the European Asylum Support Office, the European Union Satellite Centre (SATCEN) and relevant CSDP missions.
11. EUNAVFOR MED IRINI shall host a Crime Information Cell (CIC) composed of staff of relevant law enforcement authorities of Member States and of Union agencies referred to in paragraph 10, in order to facilitate the receipt, collection and transmission of information, including personal data, on the arms embargo on Libya as referred to in Article 2, on illegal exports from Libya of petroleum as referred to in Article 3, and on human smuggling and trafficking as referred to in Article 5, as well as crimes relevant to the security of the operation.
12. The processing of personal data in this context shall be carried out in accordance with the law of the flag State of the vessel on which the CIC is located and, with respect to staff of Union agencies, in accordance with the legal framework applicable to the respective agencies.
13. EUNAVFOR MED IRINI shall be supported by SATCEN and the European Union Intelligence and Situation Centre (INTCEN) in gathering information as necessary to fulfil its tasks.

**Key Defined Terms:**
- Arms embargo
- Illicit export
- Petroleum
- Human smuggling and trafficking
- Arms trafficking
- Arms and related materiel
- Personal data
- Classified information
- Security of information agreements
- Reciprocity and inclusiveness

**Entry-into-Force Date:** 31 March 2020

**Transitional or Sunset Provisions:**
EUNAVFOR MED IRINI shall end on 31 March 2021. This Decision shall be repealed as from the date of closure of the EU Operation Headquarters in accordance with the plans approved for the termination of EUNAVFOR MED IRINI and without prejudice to the procedures regarding the audit and presentation of the accounts of EUNAVFOR MED IRINI laid down in Decision (CFSP) 2015/528.

**Council Decision (EU, Euratom) 2020/2053 of 14 December 2020 on the System of Own Resources of the European Union and Repealing Decision 2014/335/EU**

**Type and Title of the Instrument:** Council Decision (EU, Euratom) 2020/2053

**Legal Basis:** Article 311(3) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) and Article 106a of the Treaty establishing the European Atomic Energy Community (Euratom)

**Subject Matter and Scope:**
This Decision establishes a new system of own resources for the European Union (EU) to ensure adequate resources for the orderly development of EU policies, while also contributing to the development of the single market and sustainable growth. The system includes traditional own resources, VAT-based own resources, and a new category of own resources based on non-recycled plastic packaging waste.

**Primary Obligations, Prohibitions, or Entitlements:**
- Traditional own resources: levies, premiums, additional or compensatory amounts, additional amounts or factors, Common Customs Tariff duties, and contributions and other duties.
- VAT-based own resources: a uniform call rate of 0.30% on the total amount of VAT receipts collected in each Member State, limited to 50% of GNI.
- Non-recycled plastic packaging waste own resources: a uniform call rate of EUR 0.80 per kilogram of non-recycled plastic packaging waste, with annual lump sum reductions for certain Member States.

**Key Defined Terms:**
- Plastic: as defined in Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006.
- Packaging waste: as defined in European Parliament and Council Directive 94/62/EC.
- Recycling: as defined in European Parliament and Council Directive 94/62/EC.

**Entry-into-Force Date:**
This Decision enters into force on the first day of the first month following receipt of the last of the notifications of the completion of the procedures for the adoption of this Decision, and applies from 1 January 2021.

**Repeal of Previous Decision:**
Decision 2014/335/EU, Euratom is repealed.

**Transition and Transitional Provisions:**
- The new system of own resources replaces the previous system introduced by Decision 2014/335/EU, Euratom.
- The new system applies from 1 January 2021, ensuring a smooth transition from the previous system.

**Key Features:**
- Simplification of the calculation of VAT-based own resources.
- Introduction of a new category of own resources based on non-recycled plastic packaging waste.
- Lump sum reductions for certain Member States to mitigate the regressive impact on national contributions.
- Increased own resources ceilings to ensure the Union's financial capacity to address the consequences of the COVID-19 crisis.
- Temporary increase in own resources ceilings to cover liabilities resulting from the borrowing of funds for the COVID-19 crisis.
- Provisions for Member States to provisionally provide cash resources to the Commission in case of insufficient liquidity.
- Repeal of previous own resources arrangements and transition to the new system.

**Decision of the European Data Protection Supervisor (EDPS) of 15 May 2020**

**Type and Title of the Instrument:** Decision

**Legal Basis:** Article 57(1)(q) of Regulation (EU) 2018/1725

**Subject Matter and Scope of Application:** The Decision sets out the Rules of Procedure for the EDPS, an independent authority responsible for ensuring compliance with the Regulation (EU) 2018/1725 and other relevant Union legal acts. The EDPS has a mission to monitor and ensure the application of the Regulation, including through investigative, corrective, authorisation, and advisory powers.

**Key Obligations, Prohibitions, or Entitlements:** The EDPS has the following key obligations:

- Act in the public's interest as an expert and independent body in the field of privacy and personal data protection.
- Act in accordance with the EDPS Ethics Framework.
- Publish strategic priorities and an Annual Report.
- Lead by example in respecting the applicable law on the protection of personal data.
- Engage openly and transparently with the media and stakeholders.
- Use state-of-the-art administrative and technical means to maximize efficiency and effectiveness.
- Implement quality management mechanisms, including internal control standards, risk management processes, and annual activity reports.
- Promote cooperation among data protection supervisory authorities and other public authorities.
- Cooperate with national supervisory authorities and international organisations.
- Appoint a Data Protection Officer (DPO) and a Transparency Officer.
- Handle complaints and facilitate amicable settlements.
- Notify institutions of personal data breaches.
- Provide guidance to Data Protection Officers and participate in meetings organized by the network of Data Protection Officers.
- Provide opinions and formal comments in response to requests from the Commission.
- Monitor the development of information and communication technologies and advise on data protection by design and data protection by default.
- Participate in research projects and serve on advisory committees.
- Refer non-compliance cases to the Court of Justice of the European Union.
- Intervene in Court of Justice of the European Union proceedings.
- Cooperate with national supervisory authorities and engage in international cooperation.
- Apply the rules for calculation of periods, dates, and time limits established under Regulation (EEC, Euratom) No 1182/71.

**Key Defined Terms:** The Decision defines terms such as 'institution,' 'EDPS,' 'GDPR,' 'EDPB,' 'EDPB secretariat,' 'Data Protection Officer,' and 'Transparency Officer.'

**Entry into Force:** The Decision enters into force on the day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.

**Repeal:** Decision 2013/504/EU of the EDPS is repealed and replaced by this Decision.

**Supplementary Measures:** The EDPS may further specify the provisions of this Decision by adopting implementing rules and supplementary measures relating to the functioning of the EDPS.

**Transitional and Sunset Provisions:** The Decision does not contain transitional or sunset provisions.

**Regulation (EU) 2020/493 of the European Parliament and of the Council**

**Type and Title of the Instrument:** Regulation (EU) 2020/493 of the European Parliament and of the Council

**Legal Basis:** Article 87(2)(a) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU)

**Subject Matter and Scope:**
This Regulation establishes the False and Authentic Documents Online (FADO) system, which contains information on authentic documents issued by Member States, the Union, and third parties, such as third countries, territorial entities, international organisations, and other entities subject to international law, and on false versions thereof. The purpose of the FADO system is to contribute to the fight against document and identity fraud by sharing information on the security features of, and potential fraud characteristics in, authentic and false documents between Member State authorities competent in the area of document fraud.

**Primary Obligations, Prohibitions, or Entitlements:**
1. The FADO system shall contain information on travel, identity, residence, and civil status documents, driving licenses, vehicle licenses, and false versions thereof.
2. Member States and the Union shall transmit information on authentic documents to the European Border and Coast Guard Agency (the 'Agency') without delay.
3. The Agency shall ensure the proper and reliable functioning of the FADO system and provide support to the competent Member State authorities in the detection of false documents.
4. The Agency shall be responsible for entering information in the FADO system in a timely and efficient manner and guaranteeing the uniformity and quality of that information.
5. The Commission and the Agency, as well as the Member State authorities competent in the area of document fraud, shall have secure access to the FADO system on a need-to-know basis.
6. The Commission shall adopt delegated acts to establish measures granting access to information stored in the FADO system to Union institutions, bodies, offices, agencies, third parties, and private entities.
7. The Agency shall apply Regulation (EU) 2018/1725 of the European Parliament and of the Council when processing personal data under this Regulation. The Agency shall only process personal data where such processing is necessary for the performance of its task of operating the FADO system.
8. The Commission shall adopt implementing acts to establish the technical architecture of the FADO system, the technical specifications for entering and storing information in the FADO system, the procedures for controlling and verifying the information contained in the FADO system, and the date of the effective implementation of the FADO system by the Agency.

**Key Defined Terms:**
- False documents: Pseudo documents, documents that have been forged and documents that have been counterfeited.
- Authentic documents: Travel, identity, residence, and civil status documents, driving licenses, vehicle licenses, laissez-passer issued by the Union, and other related official documents.
- Security features: Features of authentic documents that are used to prevent forgery.
- Fraud characteristics: Characteristics of false documents that indicate their fraudulent nature.

**Entry-into-Force Date and Transitional Provisions:**
This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union. It shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in the Member States in accordance with the Treaties. Joint Action 98/700/JHA is repealed with effect from the date of the effective implementation of the FADO system by the Agency, to be determined by means of an implementing act as referred to in point (d) of the first subparagraph of Article 6(1) of this Regulation. The General Secretariat of the Council shall transfer the information contained in the FADO system as established by Joint Action 98/700/JHA to the Agency. Member States shall agree to the transmission by the General Secretariat of the Council of the information in their ownership stored in the FADO system as established by Joint Action 98/700/JHA to the FADO system as established by this Regulation.

**Repeal and Transitional Provisions:**
Joint Action 98/700/JHA is repealed with effect from the date of the effective implementation of the FADO system by the Agency, to be determined by means of an implementing act as referred to in point (d) of the first subparagraph of Article 6(1) of this Regulation. The General Secretariat of the Council shall transfer the information contained in the FADO system as established by Joint Action 98/700/JHA to the Agency. Member States shall agree to the transmission by the General Secretariat of the Council of the information in their ownership stored in the FADO system as established by Joint Action 98/700/JHA to the FADO system as established by this Regulation.

**Entry into Force:**
This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.

**Council Regulation (EU) 2020/672 of 19 May 2020 on the establishment of a European instrument for temporary support to mitigate unemployment risks in an emergency (SURE) following the COVID-19 outbreak**

**Type and Title of the Instrument:** Council Regulation (EU) 2020/672

**Legal Basis:** Article 122(1) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU)

**Subject Matter and Scope:** This Regulation establishes the European instrument for temporary support to mitigate unemployment risks in an emergency (SURE) to address the impact of the COVID-19 outbreak and respond to its socio-economic consequences. The Instrument aims to provide financial assistance to Member States experiencing or threatened with severe economic disturbances caused by the COVID-19 outbreak, primarily for financing short-time work schemes or similar measures, and, where applicable, health-related measures.

**Primary Obligations, Prohibitions, or Entitlements:** Member States may request Union financial assistance under the Instrument where their actual and possibly also planned public expenditure has suddenly and severely increased as of 1 February 2020 due to national measures directly related to short-time work schemes and similar measures aimed at protecting employees and the self-employed. The financial assistance shall be used primarily in support of national short-time work schemes or similar measures, and, where applicable, in support of relevant health-related measures.

**Key Defined Terms:** The Regulation defines terms such as "short-time work schemes" and "health-related measures" as public programmes that allow businesses experiencing economic difficulties to temporarily reduce the hours worked by their employees, who are provided with public income support for the hours not worked, and similar measures for the self-employed.

**Entry-into-Force Date:** The Regulation enters into force on the date of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.

**Transitional or Sunset Provisions:** The Instrument is of a temporary nature and should not be used once the COVID-19 emergency has passed. The Council may extend the period of availability of the Instrument if the exceptional occurrences justifying its application continue to exist.

**Key Elements Addressed:**

- The Regulation establishes the SURE instrument to address the impact of the COVID-19 outbreak on Member States' labor markets.
- It provides financial assistance to Member States experiencing or threatened with severe economic disturbances caused by the COVID-19 outbreak.
- The financial assistance is primarily for short-time work schemes or similar measures, and, where applicable, health-related measures.
- The Instrument is temporary and should not be used once the COVID-19 emergency has passed.
- The Council may extend the period of availability of the Instrument if the exceptional occurrences justifying its application continue to exist.
- The Regulation includes prudential rules, such as maximum loan amounts, rollover of borrowings, and contributions from Member States in the form of guarantees.

**Council Regulation (EU) 2020/2094 of 14 December 2020 Establishing a European Union Recovery Instrument to Support the Recovery in the Aftermath of the COVID-19 Crisis**

**Type and Title of the Instrument:** Council Regulation (EU) 2020/2094 establishes the European Union Recovery Instrument (the "Instrument") to support the recovery in the aftermath of the COVID-19 crisis.

**Legal Basis:** The Regulation is based on Article 122 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union.

**Subject Matter and Scope:** The Instrument aims to support the recovery in the aftermath of the COVID-19 crisis by financing measures to restore employment and job creation, reinvigorate the potential for sustainable growth and employment, support businesses affected by the economic impact of the COVID-19 crisis, including small and medium-sized enterprises, and support investment in activities that are essential for strengthening sustainable growth in the Union. The measures are to be carried out under specific Union programmes and in accordance with the relevant Union acts laying down rules for those programmes.

**Primary Obligations, Prohibitions, or Entitlements:** The support under the Instrument shall finance the following measures:
- Measures to restore employment and job creation.
- Measures in the form of reforms and investments to reinvigorate the potential for sustainable growth and employment in order to strengthen cohesion among Member States and increase their resilience.
- Measures for businesses affected by the economic impact of the COVID-19 crisis, in particular measures that benefit small and medium-sized enterprises as well as support for investment in activities that are essential for strengthening sustainable growth in the Union, including direct financial investment in enterprises.
- Measures for research and innovation in response to the COVID-19 crisis.
- Measures for increasing the level of the Union’s crisis preparedness and enabling a quick and effective Union response in the event of major emergencies, including measures such as stockpiling of essential supplies and medical equipment and acquiring the necessary infrastructures for rapid crisis response.
- Measures to ensure that a just transition to a climate-neutral economy will not be undermined by the COVID-19 crisis.
- Measures to address the impact of the COVID-19 crisis on agriculture and rural development.

**Key Defined Terms:** The Regulation defines the following terms:
- "Member States" refers to all Member States of the European Union except the United Kingdom.
- "Instrument" refers to the European Union Recovery Instrument established by this Regulation.
- "Non-repayable support" refers to support provided by the Union without the obligation to repay it.
- "Repayable support" refers to support provided by the Union that is repayable.
- "Structural and cohesion programmes" refers to the structural and cohesion programmes of the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020 as reinforced until 2022.
- "Civil protection programmes" refers to programmes related to civil protection.
- "Research and innovation programmes" refers to programmes supporting research and innovation, including support through financial instruments.
- "Territories in their transition towards a climate-neutral economy" refers to territories in their transition towards a climate-neutral economy.
- "Development in rural areas" refers to development in rural areas.

**Entry-into-Force Date:** The Regulation enters into force on the day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.

**Transitional or Sunset Provisions:** The Regulation does not contain transitional or sunset provisions affecting the implementation timing of the Instrument.

**Interinstitutional Agreement on a Mandatory Transparency Register**

**Type and Title of the Instrument:** Interinstitutional Agreement

**Legal Basis:** Article 295 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU), Article 106a of the Treaty establishing the European Atomic Energy Community (EURATOM), and the 2014 Agreement between the European Parliament and the European Commission on the transparency register for organisations and self-employed individuals engaged in EU policy-making and policy implementation (OJ L 277, 19.9.2014, p. 11).

**Subject Matter and Scope of Application:** This Agreement establishes a framework and operating principles for a coordinated approach by the European Parliament, the Council of the European Union, and the European Commission (the "signatory institutions") to ensure transparent and ethical interest representation. The Agreement covers activities carried out by interest representatives (defined as any natural or legal person, or formal or informal group, association, or network) that influence the formulation or implementation of policy or legislation, or the decision-making processes of the signatory institutions or other Union institutions (together referred to as "Union institutions").

**Primary Obligations, Prohibitions, or Entitlements:** Interest representatives must:
- Identify themselves by name, registration number, and the entity or entities they work for or represent.
- Declare the interests and objectives they promote and specify the clients or members they represent, as well as the registration number of those clients or members.
- Not obtain or try to obtain information or decisions dishonestly or by use of undue pressure, improper behavior, or offensive language.
- Not abuse their registration for commercial gain or distort or misrepresent the effect of registration.
- Ensure that the information provided upon registration is complete, up-to-date, accurate, and not misleading, and agree to that information being made available in the public domain.
- Respect, and avoid obstructing, the specific access and security rules and arrangements established by the signatory institutions.
- Not induce Members of the European Parliament, members of the Commission, or staff of the Union institutions to contravene the rules and standards of behavior applicable to them.
- If employing former Members of the European Parliament, members of the Commission, or staff of the Union institutions, take the confidentiality requirements and rules applicable to those individuals after leaving the respective institution duly into account, with a view to preventing conflicts of interest.
- Where engaged in a client-intermediary relationship, ensure that the parties in such a relationship are entered in the register and that the relevant information concerning the relationship is published.
- Where outsourcing certain tasks to third parties, ensure that those parties adhere to ethical standards at least equivalent to those of registrants.
- Present supporting material demonstrating their eligibility and the accuracy of the information submitted, and cooperate sincerely and constructively with the Secretariat.
- Acknowledge that they may be subject to investigation procedures and, where applicable, measures provided for in Annex III.
- Take appropriate steps to ensure that any of their employees engaged in covered activities are informed about their commitment as registrants to observe this code of conduct.
- Inform clients or members they represent in the framework of covered activities of their commitment as registrants to observe this code of conduct.
- Respect, and avoid obstructing, the specific access and security rules and arrangements established by the signatory institutions.

**Key Defined Terms:** Interest representative, applicant, registrant, client, intermediary, client-intermediary relationship, staff, conditionality, and code of conduct.

**Entry-into-Force Date:** The Agreement entered into force on the twentieth day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union (OJ L 207, 11.6.2021, p. 1).

**Transitional and Sunset Provisions:** Registrants who were entered in the register before the date of entry into force of this Agreement shall, for a period of six months from the date of entry into force of this Agreement, be entitled to amend their registration to satisfy the new requirements resulting from this Agreement in order to remain on the register. Any investigations of alerts or complaints opened under the 2014 Agreement shall be carried out in accordance with the procedure laid down in that Agreement.

**Key Features:** The Agreement establishes a mandatory transparency register for interest representatives, with conditionality measures and complementary transparency measures to encourage registration. The Secretariat manages the register, and the Management Board oversees its implementation. The Agreement replaces the 2014 Agreement, and the effects of the 2014 Agreement cease to apply from the date of entry into force of this Agreement.

**Decision (EU) 2022/313 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 24 February 2022 providing macro-financial assistance to Ukraine**

**Type and Title of the Instrument:** Decision

**Legal Basis:** Article 212 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union

**Subject Matter and Scope of Application:** The Decision provides macro-financial assistance of a maximum amount of EUR 1.2 billion to Ukraine. The assistance is to be provided in the form of loans and is subject to the approval of the Union budget for the relevant year by the European Parliament and the Council. The assistance is to contribute to covering Ukraine's balance-of-payments needs as identified in the IMF programme. The assistance is to be implemented in accordance with Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2018/1046 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

**Primary Obligations, Prohibitions, or Entitlements:** The Ukrainian government must respect effective democratic mechanisms, including a multi-party parliamentary system, and the rule of law, and guarantee respect for human rights. The Commission and the European External Action Service shall monitor the fulfilment of the precondition throughout the life-cycle of the Union's macro-financial assistance. The Union's macro-financial assistance is to be subject to economic policy and financial conditions focusing on structural reforms and sound public finances, to be set out in a memorandum of understanding (MOU). The conditions shall aim to enhance the efficiency, transparency and accountability of the public finance management systems in Ukraine, including for the use of the Union's macro-financial assistance. The Commission shall verify, at regular intervals, that the conditions continue to be met, including whether the economic policies of Ukraine are in accordance with the objectives of the Union's macro-financial assistance. The Union's macro-financial assistance shall be disbursed in two equal instalments, each of which shall consist of a loan. The timeframe for the disbursement of each instalment shall be laid down in the MOU. The release of the second instalment shall not, in principle, take place earlier than three months after the release of the first instalment. The Union's macro-financial assistance shall be implemented under direct management and shall be subject to economic policy conditions, to be set out in a MOU, which shall include a timeframe for the fulfilment of those conditions. The conditions shall be consistent with the agreements or understandings referred to in Article 1(3), including the macroeconomic adjustment and structural reform programmes implemented by Ukraine with the support of the IMF.

**Key Defined Terms:** The Decision does not define any key terms.

**Entry-into-Force Date:** The Decision enters into force on the day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.

**Transitional or Sunset Provisions:** The Decision does not contain any transitional or sunset provisions.
